_doc: goindex's candidate-extractor tables (po-av01j.219). They are JUDGMENT about
what is worth looking at, not code: they decide what is retrieved, never what a
match means. Coverage is resolution over what these tables retrieve, so a
surface missing here is invisible to every number the scanner reports.
known_unretrieved is the completeness measure: I/O the tables do not retrieve,
counted per scan as existing-but-not-retrieved so the gap is a number.
Moving an entry from known_unretrieved into io_methods is a retrieval change
and needs specs for the new sites, or every one of them abstains as no_spec.
bound_constructors selects the unsized-construction inventory: package-level
functions that build an object which takes a bound (class pool, queue, cache)
or that read a whole body (class read). It says where to look, not what a
bound is: the packet lists the setters and options seen, and a
construction-bound spec judges them. io.ReadAll is in both lists on purpose:
it is still not a G1 call site, and it is an unsized read.

known_unretrieved.why: reads a whole body with no size or time bound of its own; po-av01j.149 found three on nats-server that no number reported
the deprecated spelling of io.ReadAll, still common in older trees
